# WO-2026-08-11-03 — A choice he has already made is found under a different spelling

## The defect

WP-B15-13 (`051050f`) made product MATCHING separator-blind via `squashMatchText`
(`skill/termMatch.js:164`, exported at `:396`), so `VANISH PRETREAT GEL` now resolves to the
household regular `Vanish Pre-Treat Gel`. **It did not touch `pipeline/`.**

A remembered choice is keyed on `pipeline/keys.js` `normaliseTerm` (`:193`) — a **different** rule,
which turns punctuation into spaces rather than removing it — persisted as
`asdair.remembered_choice.choice_term`, stamped `keys.normaliseTerm@1`, and looked up by **SQL exact
equality**: `choice_term = ANY($2::text[])` (`rememberedChoice.js:134`, executed at `:434`).

So:

| | |
|---|---|
| `normaliseTerm('VANISH PRETREAT GEL')` | `vanish pretreat gel` |
| `normaliseTerm('Vanish Pre-Treat Gel')` | `vanish pre treat gel` |

**Same product after B15-13. Two different memory keys.** The answer he gave under one spelling is
not found under the other, and he is asked again next week.

**It is worse than a miss: it is an INVISIBLE miss.** `memories.get(term)` returns `undefined`, and
because `memories.has(term)` is false, `rememberedChoice.js:588` emits **no `refused` entry** — so
the step report shows nothing at all. `resolveFromMemory` is never even reached.

**Note the happy accident that makes this cheap:** `squashMatchText` applied to *either* normalised
form yields the same string, because squashing removes the separators that the two rules disagree
about. You do not need to re-derive anything from the raw text.

## ⛔ The obvious fix is the wrong one, and it is a REFUSE condition

**Do NOT make `keys.normaliseTerm` separator-blind.** It is deliberately separate and it is
**data-shaped**: it mints `question_key` via `questionKeyFor` (`keys.js:260`, pinned byte-for-byte at
`:253-258`, with live rows keyed by it) and the ledger `idempotency_key` via
`commands.js:340 → commandKeyFor`. Changing it changes the identity of persisted keys — a worse
class of defect than the one being fixed. `skill/planner.js` keeps its own for the same reason.

Migration `018_remembered_choice.sql:120-133` also says, of the memory key: **"DO NOT MAKE THIS KEY
FUZZY TO CLOSE THAT."** That instruction stands and this order does not overturn it — you are not
making the key fuzzy, you are making the LOOKUP aware of one specific, already-ruled equivalence.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — The fix applies WP-B15-13's rule at the lookup, and reuses the exported function.** Use
`squashMatchText` from `skill/termMatch.js` — do **not** write a second separator-blind
implementation. A third spelling of this rule in a file whose whole problem is that it holds a second
normaliser would be the same defect wearing another hat. `pipeline/` is ESM and `skill/` is CJS;
`requireCjs` is the established bridge (precedent: `runPipeline.js:98`).

**AC2 — The live case resolves, end to end through the planning path.** A memory written under one
spelling is found and applied when the same product arrives spelled with different separators, and
**no question is opened for that line**. Use the real `VANISH PRETREAT GEL` / `Vanish Pre-Treat Gel`
pair — it is the case that actually happened to Warwick.

**AC3 — Every existing refusal still refuses.** `resolveFromMemory` (`rememberedChoice.js:472`) is
headed `⛔ THIS IS THE FUNCTION THAT MUST NEVER BECOME CLEVER. ⛔` and that stands. All three
refusals must still fire: fewer than two candidates this week; the chosen id not among this week's
candidates; the chosen regular no longer active. **A separator-blind lookup must not become a fuzzy
lookup** — a misspelling is still a miss, exactly as `termMatch.test.js:247` requires for matching.
Prove at least one refusal still refuses *via the new lookup path*, not only via the old one.

**AC4 — A digit-to-digit separator is still never removed.** `1.5L` must not become `15L`.
`squashMatchText` already guarantees this (`termMatch.js:164-172`, `isDigit` at `:174`); assert it
holds through your lookup so a future edit cannot quietly lose it.

**AC5 — No schema change without coming back.** The live table holds exactly ONE row, so there is no
migration burden. Prefer a solution needing no DDL — an in-process comparison over the household's
rows is entirely reasonable at this scale. **If you conclude a stored column or expression index is
genuinely required, STOP and return a CLARIFY**: that is a Silas decision and a separate gated live
apply, and a second blocked migration would stall this session. If you do choose an in-process
comparison, bound it explicitly and say what happens as the table grows.

**AC6 — The invisible miss becomes visible.** Whatever shape you choose, a memory that exists but is
not used must produce a `refused` entry with a reason, rather than vanishing at
`rememberedChoice.js:588`. A silent miss is how this survived unnoticed in the first place.

**AC7 — Mutation proof, both directions, with the source proven to have changed.** For AC2 and AC3
separately: mutate the delivered logic, prove the test goes RED, restore, prove GREEN. **Assert the
source file actually changed before believing any red** — a CRLF no-op silently produces a false
green here and has done so four times on this estate. Report executed counts for every run; `0
executed` is a FAILURE. Restore in a `finally`, or mutate a copy.

**AC8 — No new mechanism, no new dependency, no live database.** `live_authority: none`,
`credential_scope: none`.
